sections.h2: Why does selling in Pompano Beach differ from selling elsewhere in Broward?
sections.html:
Pompano Beach is a beach city in the northern part of Broward County, and the city's own resident page says it spans over 25 square miles halfway between Miami and Palm Beach. The same page says residents number over 101,400 for most of the year and then top 150,000 once part-time owners return for the winter.

That seasonal pulse shapes a sale. Showings pick up when snowbirds are in town, and a vacant house can sit quietly through summer. Owners with a house that needs work, a tenant or an unpaid lien usually weigh three paths.

  • Listing with an agent, which brings repair requests, open houses and a lender-dependent closing date.
  • Selling to a neighbor or relative without an agent, which leaves pricing and paperwork to you.
  • Accepting a cash offer for the house in its current shape, with the closing day set by the seller.

sections.h2: How did Pompano Beach get its name and its housing mix?
sections.html:
The city's historical pages say a survey crew working for the canal and railway companies around 1880 wrote the word pompano on a map, and the settlement kept it. The town incorporated in 1908, and Beach joined the name on June 16, 1947, after the oceanfront settlement was annexed.

Growth came in layers. The Census Bureau counted 99,845 people in 2010 and 112,046 in 2020, then estimated 117,211 for July 2025. Older single-family blocks, mid-century duplexes and newer condo and townhome projects now share the same city, so a flat citywide price tells you little about one address.

The city markets its 1,000-foot fishing pier, redeveloped beachside fishing village and the early-1900s Hillsboro Lighthouse near the inlet. Properties close to the water raise flood-zone and insurance questions, so gather your policy, any elevation certificate and permits for roof, window or seawall work before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What does the Broward homestead exemption mean when I sell in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
It ends with your ownership. Broward's property appraiser states that the seller's exemptions do not continue beyond the year of the sale, so a buyer who will live in the house files a new application.

Broward lists a filing window that closes on March 1 each year, with a hard late-filing cutoff of September 20, 2027 for the 2027 year. The office also warns that renting the house out would likely cost an owner the exemption and that unreported changes can bring back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

Because Florida re-values a property after a change of ownership, a buyer's first bill often runs above yours. The Department of Revenue says a sale, foreclosure or title transfer starts that reset, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. Ask Broward's exemption division to confirm anything unusual about your parcel.

  • Hold on to the annual receipt Broward mails each January.
  • Cancel the exemption on a house you no longer occupy.
  • Ask about portability if you are moving to another Florida homestead within three tax years.

sections.h2: How will Amendment 3 touch a Pompano Beach sale?
sections.html:
Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and it takes effect January 1, 2027. The Volusia County Property Appraiser's explanation says it raises the non-school homestead exemption to up to $150,000 in 2027 and up to $250,000 in 2028, and lowers the non-homestead assessment cap from 10 percent to 5 percent.

That office also says implementing legislation has to settle some details. For a seller, the practical point is that a future owner-occupant may value the larger exemption, while a landlord buying a rental weighs the lower cap. Ask Broward's property appraiser how the rules will reach your parcel.

sections.h2: What costs and paperwork come with a deed in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
The deed carries Florida's documentary stamp tax, set at 70 cents per $100 of consideration for every county but Miami-Dade. The revenue department adds that every party to the document is liable, so the purchase contract settles who pays.

The Broward clerk records the deed and collects that tax. Under section 28.24 the clerk's first-page recording charge is $5.00 and each additional page is $4.00, before extra per-page technology charges, so request a current quote.

  • Request a payoff statement from every mortgage and lien holder.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the Broward tax bill.
  • Check city permit and code records for open items.
  • Line up two witnesses for the deed signing, which Florida requires for land conveyances.

sections.h2: What if the Pompano Beach house has tenants, a foreclosure case or an heir?
sections.html:
Each situation sells, but each has its own clock. For a tenant on a month-to-month term, section 83.57 requires notice of at least 30 days before the end of a monthly period; for unpaid rent, section 83.56 starts with a three-day written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays.

In a foreclosure, section 45.031 has the clerk hold the sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the lender agrees to longer, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A sale that closes first can protect your equity.

For an inherited house, summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner died over two years ago, under section 735.201. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the revenue department as not taxable for stamps.

faqs.q: Can a cash sale close sooner than a listing in Pompano Beach?
faqs.a: Often yes, since no lender appraisal is involved. Title still has to be clear, liens paid off and the deed signed before two witnesses and recorded with the Broward clerk.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamps on a Pompano Beach sale?
faqs.a: The contract decides. The Department of Revenue says every party to the document is liable for the tax, which is 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Broward's property appraiser says the seller's exemptions stop with the year of sale, and the buyer files a new application, due by March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell while I am behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the sale closes before the foreclosure sale. The clerk usually sets that sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment, so act early.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded in Pompano Beach?
faqs.a: With the Broward County clerk, who records the instrument and collects documentary stamp tax at that moment. Bring the signed deed and the recording fee.
